key_insight: A physics-informed graph neural network can decode the surface code by learning a syndrome-adaptive discrete Poisson metric and then extracting a single topological scalar that captures the logical error signal.
engineering_relevance: This provides an exact, parameter-free readout that is simpler than full-field decoding yet can match strong decoders on rotated surface code data, making it attractive for scalable quantum error correction pipelines.
method: Build a syndrome graph and impose a discrete Poisson equation as a hard physics prior.
Learn edge weights with a graph encoder, then solve differentiably for node potentials and edge currents.
Read out the logical decision from the difference in current drained by the two code boundaries linked by the logical operator.
evidence_signal: On the rotated surface code with circuit-level depolarising noise, the single topological scalar matches the best full-field readout, and the advantage appears stronger at larger code distances.
watch_item: The approach relies on a learned metric and boundary-specific pairing, so performance may depend on how well the solver, topology, and boundary conditions are implemented for each code geometry.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Graph Neural Networks for Surface Code Decoding via Discrete Exterior Calculus
